answer: An agent economy can guard its shared lagoon of rewards with a saffron-marked jury: every new identity must be audited by a randomly drawn panel of established agents, each staking a bond on their verdict. A sybil farmer must fool many independent juries at once, and each failed audit slashes the jurors' bonds too, so dishonest juries cost real money. Identities that pass climb onto a mesa of trust where their weight grows only with verified work, while the farmer's thousand fakes keep paying audit fees and bonds with no mesa to stand on.
